title: Compare genomic interval overlaps

sources.locator: Default behavior; Intersecting against MULTIPLE -b files
bedtools intersect; Reporting the original feature in each file; Counting the number of overlapping features; Find features that DO NOT overlap

scientific_use: Find shared genomic bases or features between interval sets, count overlaps, retain original query/database records, enforce overlap fractions, and select non-overlapping features. The tutorial demonstrates CpG-island/exon comparisons; example usage describes reads/genes, exons/repeats, and disease variants/segmental duplications.
tool_role_basis: The documented work applies the existing bedtools intersect command to BED/BAM/GFF/VCF feature inputs; the task concerns analysis of intervals, not implementation of the overlap algorithm.
inputs: Two or more genome feature sets (BED/GFF/VCF, and in supported modes BAM), with coordinates and optional feature metadata; A is the query and B is the comparison set. Biological example: CpG islands and RefSeq exons; tutorial data include human genomic intervals.
outputs: Intersected shared intervals or original A/B records, overlap base counts, per-A overlap counts, or A records without a B overlap depending on options; tabular genome-feature files.
dependencies: bedtools2 command-line executable
Compatible chromosome naming and coordinate conventions; sorted inputs for -sorted mode
UNIX shell piping/redirection for the documented compositions
evidence: The tutorial explicitly runs cpg.bed against exons.bed and shows overlap intervals, original records, overlap bases, counts, and non-overlapping CpG islands.
The example-usage section describes alignment/gene, exon/repeat, and SV/segmental-duplication overlap questions.
limitations: Tutorial BED assets are referenced via historical external URLs; current availability, genome assembly, exact source versions, redistribution rights, and reproducibility were not verified.
The docs establish command behavior, not a validated task or execution result.

title: Test interval overlap enrichment with Fisher's exact test

sources.locator: Opening example; Evaluation; Usage and option summary

scientific_use: Assess whether two interval sets overlap more than expected given their coverage and genome size. The command reports overlap/unique counts, an estimated number of possible intervals, a contingency table and left/right/two-tail p-values; docs caution that the possible-interval heuristic can inflate significance and recommend simulation validation.
tool_role_basis: The documented unit applies bedtools fisher and its built-in statistical routine to interval sets; task work is interpretation/analysis, not algorithm development.
inputs: Two chromosome/start-sorted BED/GFF/VCF feature sets and genome chromosome sizes; overlap criteria may include fraction and strand constraints.
outputs: Counts, estimated possible-interval count, contingency table, Fisher p-values for tails, and ratio.
dependencies: bedtools2 executable; sorted feature inputs; genome size file
Interpretation must account for the documentation's estimated possible-interval heuristic; simulation is suggested for validating low p-values
evidence: fisher.rst gives a three-feature/two-feature synthetic example with a one-chromosome genome and contrasts 500-base and 60-base universes.
The Evaluation section describes 1000 shuffle simulations of 3000 intervals of lengths 20 to 5250 against canonical chr1 genes and notes inflation.
limitations: The evaluation's canonical-gene input and generated intervals are not identified as available assets in the inspected docs; it is not a reusable dataset record.
Null-model assumptions, analytical approximation, and statistical validity for a proposed task require author review; no execution performed.

title: Compare spatial proximity distributions of genomic intervals
source_kind: command documentation with named biological examples

sources.locator: Purpose and Favorov et al citation; Default behavior and exon/AluY and exon/GERP examples

scientific_use: Measure the distribution of relative distances between each A interval and its two closest B intervals, revealing spatial association when direct intersections are uncommon. The source contrasts RefSeq exons versus AluY repeats (roughly uniform distribution) and versus GERP conserved elements (many zero-distance overlaps), and notes self-comparison yields zero distances.
tool_role_basis: The documentation describes applying the existing reldist command to scientific feature sets and interpreting its summary/detail output.
inputs: Two BED/GFF/VCF interval sets; documentation examples use data/refseq.chr1.exons.bed.gz as A and data/aluY.chr1.bed.gz or data/gerp.chr1.bed.gz as B.
outputs: Relative-distance frequency distribution over 0.0 to 0.5, or per-A relative distances with -detail.
dependencies: bedtools2 executable
Biologically compatible assembly/chromosome and coordinate systems across feature sets
evidence: reldist.rst explicitly supplies the two example invocations and resulting distributions and defines interpretation of uniform versus low-distance-enriched distributions.
The documentation cites Favorov et al., PLoS Computational Biology 2012, doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002529.
limitations: Repository filenames and docs identify data roles but do not establish assembly, original study/accession, release, licensing, or the precise processing history.
Reported values are documentation examples, not recomputed or validated here.

title: Compare fetal-tissue DNase hypersensitivity interval sets
source_kind: multi-command scientific workflow and tutorial analysis

sources.locator: Principal component analysis; A Jaccard statistic for all 400 pairwise comparisons

scientific_use: Compare overlap similarity among DNase hypersensitivity intervals from fetal tissue samples using bedtools jaccard, form a 20-by-20 pairwise similarity matrix, then explore sample relationships with PCA or a heatmap. The tutorial gives separate same-tissue and cross-tissue examples and notes heatmaps are more informative for this distance-like statistic.
tool_role_basis: The workflow applies bedtools jaccard to study intervals and then uses a custom make-matrix.py plus R PCA/heatmap code to compose and analyze the pairwise measurements; it is an analysis workflow rather than a modification of bedtools itself.
inputs: 20 tissue-specific, merged BED interval files from the tutorial's fetal DNaseI archive; examples name two Heart samples and a Skin fibroblast bicep sample. Pairwise comparisons operate on those derived `.merge.bed` inputs.
outputs: 400 pairwise Jaccard values, a 20-by-20 matrix and PCA/heatmap visualizations of tissue/sample similarity.

GNU parallel for the tutorial's parallel all-pairs stage
